## {{< var wip >}} Configuration file

In addition to passing configuration options via command line flags or
Python parameters, Flower can be configured via the `pyproject.toml` or `.flower.toml` files. The
advantage of doing so is that the formatting can be easier for complex
multi-page documentation sites and that options that are frequently used
can be set once instead of included each time Flower is called from the
Terminal or Python.

### Examples

#### Using a built-in style

```{.toml filename="pyproject.toml"}
[tool.seedcase-flower]
style="quarto-resource-listings"
```

Running `build` with this configuration file builds metadata files
with Quarto for the Data Package in the current working directory. The
chosen style, `quarto-resource-listings`, splits the metadata into several files.
See the [Outputs](/docs/design/outputs.qmd) page for details on the built-in style options.

#### Using a custom style

```{.toml filename="pyproject.toml"}
[tool.flower]
style="custom"

[[tool.flower.section]]
template="1st-page.html"
content="package"

[[tool.flower.section]]
template="2nd-page.html"
content=[
    "contributors",
    "licenses",
]
```

Running `build` with this configuration file builds the Data Package metadata files
in html format in the current working directory.
The custom style creates one page with the package
metadata and a second page with info on the contributors and license.
Both pages are created using a custom HTML template.
